recipes.name: Arnhemse meisjes
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53392. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Take your puff pastry from the freezer and defrost.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: Sprinkle some flour on the kitchen counter. Stack the sheets of puff pastry on top of each other and roll them out with a rolling pin. You want those five sheets to end up being as thin as one sheet.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Using a round or oval form press into the puff pastry and try to be as economical doing that as possible. You want to have as many cookies as you can.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Mix the vanilla sugar with the cinnamon, cardemom and limezest in a little bowl

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Remove the flour from the counter and sprinkle with a bit of the sugar mix.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Brush your puff pastry with a little bit of eggwash and than dip into the sugar mix and roll them softly to press the sugar in.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Put your sugary puff pastry on a baking sheet (greased or with baking paper) and leave the dough to rest for about 20 to 25 minutes. this will make the cookies even crisper.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Preheat the oven in the meantime to 180 C and put the baking tray in the oven.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: bake the cookies golden brown in about 25 minutes and make sure the sugar is caramelised nicely

steps.title: Step 10
steps.instruction: And voila, Girls from Arnhem with an Almeerse twist

steps.title: Step 11
steps.instruction: Voila, Arnhemse Meisjes met een Almeerse twist.

recipes.name: Arroz con Leche Recipe

recipes.name: Baghlaw-e-Khanagi
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53396. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Place flour in a bowl, and create a hole in the middle of the flour. Whisk eggs, and then pour whisked eggs into the well.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: Add milk, and combine. Then, stir in the ground walnuts, baking powder and cardamom, and add to the mixture. Fold ingredients into the mixture until it forms an elastic dough consistency.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Take dough and with a rolling pin, roll out into a thin rectangle on a clean surface. Then, from the longest side of the rectangle, fold the dough into 3cm-wide lines, until the dough is fully rolled in a long line. Cut folded dough horizontally into 3cm pieces

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Heat a deep pan of the vegetable oil, and wait till it reaches frying temperature. Whilst you are waiting. Fill a deep pan with 1 litre of water, and bring to the boil.  Then, pour in the sugar, and stir gently until it becomes thick and syrup-like. Turn down the heat and leave to simmer.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Carefully lower each piece of dough into the frying oil. Fry until golden brown.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: When golden brown, take the Baghlaw pieces out of the oil, and place them into the sugar syrup to coat.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Remove from the syrup and whilst still warm, sprinkle with ground walnuts, so they stick to the Baghlaw.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Leave to cool. Then, enjoy with your friends and family!

recipes.name: Breadfruit in Butter Sauce Recipe
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53454. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Captain William Bligh was chosen to lead an expedition to the South Seas to bring the breadfruit to the Caribbean.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: His devotion to the breadfruit saplings and neglect of his crew’s water needs lead to the famous “Mutiny on the Bounty” on his first attempt. Cast overboard; Captain Bligh made his way hundreds of miles to safety in an open boat.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: On his second attempt in 1793, he sailed into Jamaica’s Port Royal Harbour with a ship so crowded with beautiful leafy breadfruit saplings that the Jamaicans rowed out toward “the ship that has bush.”

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Today large, lush breadfruit trees grow throughout the Caribbean, bearing the football-like starchy staple that has kept hunger away from many a door. Breadfruit may be difficult to find outside the Caribbean.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: You will need the following ingredients:

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: 1/2 medium breadfruit

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: 1/2 small onion

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: 1 tablespoon olive oil

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: 4 oz/125g butter

steps.title: Step 10
steps.instruction: 3 medium onions, cut into rings

steps.title: Step 11
steps.instruction: 1 tablespoon garlic finely chopped

steps.title: Step 12
steps.instruction: 1 medium 16floz/500ml tin whole tomatoes, drained and sliced

steps.title: Step 13
steps.instruction: 1/4 cup or 3 tablespoons parsley, diced

steps.title: Step 14
steps.instruction: 1 tablespoon lime juice

recipes.name: CAFE LA LLAVE ESPRESSO ICE CREAM
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53544. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: A note about the espresso: I like using the fine ground espresso brick and making the coffee in a regular moka pot, but you can certainly also use the Nespresso style capsules if you have that type of espresso maker. FULL DISCLOSURE: I personally prefer the decaf espresso, which the Cafe La Llave brand makes to perfection. The ice cream flavor holds either way.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: In a medium saucepan, heat the cream, milk, sugar and salt over medium heat; whisking to dissolve the sugar (this should take about 4 to 5 minutes).

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: In a separate bowl, whisk the egg yolks.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Gradually pour about 1 cup of the hot milk mixture into the egg yolk bowl, while continually whisking. Do this carefully to temper the eggs. (You’re not cooking them.)

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Add the tempered egg yolk mix back into the pan while whisking until it just comes to a simmer.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Remove the pan from the heat, then add the vanilla extract and espresso.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: you can use any ice cream maker. It doesn’t have to be fancy.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Use between 2 and 4 shots of espresso (regular or decaf) depending on how strong you like the coffee flavor in the ice cream. I think about 3 shots is ideal.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: This recipe will yield about 1 quart of ice cream.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.instruction: Please sit back and enjoy your espresso ice cream. Also, stay cool. You’re welcome

recipes.name: Cinnamon Roll Cookies
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53462. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: 1) In a large bowl, combine the butter and caster sugar until creamy. Add the egg and a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: 2) Stir into a buttery mixture. Add the sifted flour.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: 3) Whisk well. You should end up with a smooth dough. Cover it with a piece of plastic wrap and put the dough in the fridge for 15 minutes to chill and set.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: 4) In the meantime combine the cassonade (or brown sugar) and the cinnamon.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: 5) Transfer the dough onto a floured surface and knead it for a minute. Add extra flour if necessary. Roll the dough out gently into a nice rectangle. It should be about ⅕-inch (5 mm) thick. Sprinkle with the sugary cinnamon mixture.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: 6) Carefully start rolling the dough up. If it is too sticky, put it in the fridge again for a couple of minutes. Wrap it up tightly in plastic wrap.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: 7) Put it in the fridge for 30 minutes to chill and set. After that, remove the cling film and cut the dough roll into even slices.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: 8) Place the slices on a baking paper lined baking tray. Bake the cookies in a preheated oven at 356°F (180°C) for 14 to 16 minutes.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: 9) Let the baked cinnamon roll cookies cool down fully before eating or wrapping them up.

recipes.name: Coconut Natilla Recipe

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Place the rest of the milk and cinnamon sticks in a medium pot and bring the mixture to boil over medium-low heat. When the milk is a little warm, but not boiling, add the coconut mixture.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: When the milk starts boiling, add the condensed milk, sugar and salt. Stir well with a wooden spoon. Add the milk and cornstarch mixture and continue stirring constantly.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Add the vanilla extract. Reduce the heat to low and continue stirring until the Natilla thickens, about 10 to 20 minutes. Add the butter, stir and remove from the heat. Discard the cinnamon sticks. Ladle into a serving dish or individual custard cups. Sprinkle cinnamon powder on top and let it cool at room temperature for at least 2 hours. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

recipes.name: Dutch doughnuts
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53393. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Place the flour in a large bowl and add the yeast and sugar. If the milk is cold make sure to heat it to lukewarm. Mix your flour mixture bit by bit with the milk until you have a smooth batter. Add the salt and mix with a wooden spoon till the batter is smooth and liquidy.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: Cover with a clean tea towel and leave in a warm spot for about an hour to rise.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Heat your deep fryer or add the oil to a large pot. The oil should be a t 180˚C (350˚F) for best results.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Before starting stir your batter through and scoop the batter with two spoons or with an ice cream scoop. Let it drop into the oil carefully. It is easiest to do this if you dip your spoons or scoop into the oil before dipping into the batter. That way it will slide of the spoons easily. Don't over crowd the fryer to prevent the oil cooling down too quickly and everything sticking together. Once one side is golden brown it usually turns around to the other side automatically. If not help it along with two forks.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Take the balls out once golden brown and leave to drain on a piece of kitchen paper.

steps.title: Step 5

recipes.name: Handesh – Bangladeshi rice flour and date molasses cakes
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53452. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Add the molasses to a large mixing bowl and begin by pouring 300ml of water to start with and whisk together. The texture of Bangladeshi molasses varies from a thick syrup to slightly set. I use brands such as Zilani or Akza. If the set is very syrupy (like golden syrup) you will only require 300–325ml of water

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Pour in the flours and spices (if using) and whisk for 3–5 minutes, until you have a smooth batter. You need to check carefully for lumps, as they prevent the handesh from rising and will cause them to split. Cover the batter and rest for 2 hours

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: After 2 hours, thoroughly whisk the batter until smooth, as the rice flour will have settled at the bottom of the bowl. The batter should have a fairly thick consistency, yet remain loose enough to pour – similar to thick pancake or waffle batter. It should form ribbons as you drag the whisk though it

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Take a cast-iron korai or wok and add enough oil to half-fill the pan, or enough to deep-fry and turn the heat to high. Once the oil is hot reduce the heat to low–medium. Drop in a teaspoon of batter to test the oil – if it rises slowly to the surface the oil is ready

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: Pour batter in a quick steady stream into the centre of the pan, preferably using a pyrex jug with a pouring spout (About 45ml of batter for each cake). It should rise to the surface in about 15–20 seconds and slowly puff up. If it rises too quickly, just turn the heat down slightly. Cook for 45 seconds, or until the underside is golden. Carefully turn over and cook for a further 30–45 seconds, until golden. Make sure to not let excess batter drip into the pan as this may prevent the cakes from rising and always fry one at a time

steps.title: Step 11
steps.instruction: If the batter splits while frying, whisk in 2 tablespoons of flour to the mixture and try again. You should be creating handesh which are about the size of a digestive biscuit

steps.title: Step 13
steps.instruction: Use a slotted spoon to remove the handesh and place on kitchen towel with frilled edge facing down while you continue frying the reaming batter. This helps retain the shape of the cakes

recipes.name: Leche Asada
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53519. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.instruction: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

steps.title: Step 3

steps.instruction: Remove the dough from the mixer bowl and form into a ball. Lightly mist the bowl with oil and replace the ball of dough into it. Cover the bowl and let rise in a warm place, 1 to 1½ hours, until doubled.

I also like to set up a drying rack set over a paper-towel-lined sheet pan to drain the doughnuts on, so they stay crispy. You can also prep a plate with paper towels if you don't want to bother.

steps.title: Step 9

recipes.name: Old-fashioned Danish Apple Trifle
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53551. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Peel and cut the apples into cubes. Discard the cores. Transfer apple cubes to a saucepan with water, vanilla and lemon juice. Bring apples to a boil, cover and reduce heat to medium-low.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: Add the sugar to taste after the apples release their juices. The amount of sugar depends on the tartness of the apples and your preferred level of sweetness. Remember that the breadcrumb mixture and whipped cream are also sweet, so it is okay if the apple sauce is still a bit tart.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Cook the apples for about 15 minutes until you have a coarse apple sauce. If you prefer, cook the apples longer for a finer consistency.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Refrigerate the applesauce.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Breadcrumbs mixture:

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Melt butter in a pan. The butter must not brown. Add breadcrumbs and sugar and stir to combine.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Slowly toast the mixture as you stir with a spatula. Do not heat the mixture for too long – it only takes a short time to make.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Once the breadcrumbs are lightly golden, remove from the pan and cool on a sheet of baking paper.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: Assembling the apple trifle:

steps.title: Step 10
steps.instruction: Do not assemble the trifle until right before serving. Otherwise, the rasp will become soggy. Serve the trifle in individual small glasses or a large glass bowl.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.instruction: Lightly whip the double cream.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.instruction: Layer the ingredients in the glasses or bowl, starting with breadcrumbs in the bottom, followed by chilled apple sauce and breadcrumbs again. You can make several layers of breadcrumbs and apple sauce, then top with a generous layer of whipped cream. Serve immediately.

steps.instruction: Sift the flour and cornstarch and add to the mixture. Fold this gently into the mixture; you don’t want all the air you whipped in to disappear.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Pour the batter into a greased baking pan. Bake the cake base at 180°C/350°F (conventional oven) for 30 minutes. The cake is done when you press lightly on the top and it springs back. Allow the cake to cool in the pan for a few minutes before removing it to a cake rack.

Then roll out the dough and transfer to the pan. Bake in the middle of the oven for approximately 25 minutes. Prepare the vanilla custard while the dough bakes.

steps.title: Step 5

recipes.name: Tamal De Maicena
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53535. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Preheat the oven at 350F.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: In a non-stick medium pot, add the milk, butter, sugar, and vanilla; bring to a boil, and reduce heat to low.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: In a large bowl, add the eggs and the cornstarch and mix well. Slowly add 1 cup of the milk mixture, mixing constantly to temper the eggs. Keep adding more milk until the mixture is soft and has no lumps.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Add the mixture to the pot SLOWLY and mix constantly using a wooden spoon.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Keep cooking and mixing for a few more minutes until the mixture gets thick, you will know when it is ready when passing a spoon at the bottom of the pot creates a line that separates the mixture.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Remove from heat and pour into the pyrex (no need to grease it ( I use an 11 by 8-inch pyrex).

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Cover with foil and cook for approximately 50 min. Remove the foil after 30 min of cooking to allow the top to get a light brown color.  Let it cool completely before serving.

recipes.name: Traditional Dutch rice tart (rijstevlaai)
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53391. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 180°C. For the dough, mix flour and sugar in a bowl. Heat the 100 grams of milk to lukewarm and dissolve the yeast in it. Let stand for a while until it starts to bubble. Then add to the flour along with the coconut oil and mix into a smooth dough. Let rise for 30 minutes, covered, in a warm place.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: Meanwhile, make the rice pudding by putting the rice with sugar, milk and vanilla extract in a saucepan. Add the cardamom, star anise and cinnamon. Bring to a boil and cook, stirring constantly. Take out the spices. In a small bowl, mix baking soda with lemon juice/apple vinegar. Stir well until baking soda is dissolved, then mix into the rice pudding.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Roll out the dough on a floured work surface (it is very sticky, but don’t stress it will be fine) and line the bottom and edges of a greased mold with it. Spread the rice pudding over the bottom and bake for about 25 to 30 minutes.

recipes.name: Zeeuwse bolussen
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53394. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Place the dried yeast, milk and sugar in the bowl of your food processor. Mix and let stand for a few minutes until it begins to foam.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: Then add the flour, egg, butter, salt, 1 tsp of cinnamon and cardamom and process until smooth.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Form the dough into a ball, cover the bowl and let it rise for 1 hour or until it has doubled in size.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Mix the caster sugar with 1 tablespoon of cinnamon, pour over the dough and roll it in.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Form 10 equal balls (about 75 grams each) and let them “sweat” for a while. The sugar will dissolve a little. When you roll them again later, the rest of the dough will absorb the sugar better.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Then roll the ball into a strand about 35-40 centimeters long while rolling through the powdered sugar.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Fold the strand around one end and tuck the other end under the bolus. Push something between the roll to secure the end.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Place on a baking sheet lined with a baking sheet, cover with plastic wrap and let them rise for ½-1 hour.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 250 degrees Celsius/480 Fahrenheit top and bottom heat

steps.title: Step 10
steps.instruction: Bake the Zeeland Boluses for about 8 minutes until done. Be careful – if you bake them too long, they will get dry and you will want something sticky 😉 .

steps.title: Step 11
steps.instruction: Let them cool out of the oven for 1 minute, then turn them over and let them cool further (on a wire rack if necessary). Enjoy!
